questions.question: In the absence of a partnership deed, partners are entitled to:
options: B) Salary as per industry standard
C) No salary, no interest on capital, profits shared equally
questions.explanation: Per Indian Partnership Act 1932: no salary, no IOC, profits shared equally.

questions.question: Under fluctuating capital method, the Capital Account shows:
options: D) All changes including profit share and drawings
questions.explanation: Under fluctuating method, Capital Account reflects all adjustments.

questions.question: A partner withdraws Rs. 10,000 at the beginning of each half-year. Rate = 8% p.a. Interest on drawings for the year is:
questions.explanation: Average period = (12+6)/2 = 9 months. Total = 20,000. Interest = 20,000 x 8% x 9/12 = Rs. 1,200.

questions.question: A partner advances Rs. 20,000 to the firm. In the absence of a deed, the interest payable on this advance is:
questions.explanation: Per Indian Partnership Act 1932, interest on advances by partners is payable at 6% p.a.

questions.question: A gets 10% commission on net profit before charging commission. Net profit = Rs. 2,00,000. A commission is:
Partners X and Y share profits equally. Salary to Y Rs. 36,000 was omitted. The correction entry will:
options: A) Decrease X capital by Rs. 18,000
B) Decrease Y capital by Rs. 18,000
D) Increase Y capital by Rs. 36,000
questions.explanation: Y salary = Rs. 36,000. Reduces profit shared equally (Rs. 18,000 each). Net: X loses 18,000.

questions.question: P and Q share profits 3:2. R is admitted for 1/4 share guaranteed minimum Rs. 60,000. Firm profit = Rs. 2,00,000. Deficiency borne by P alone. P deficiency contribution is:
Normal profit = Rs. 25,000. Actual average profit = Rs. 40,000. Goodwill is valued at 5 years purchase of super profit. Goodwill value is:
M and N share profits 4:3. They admit O for 1/7 share. The sacrifice ratio of M and N is:
questions.explanation: In absence of specific agreement, existing partners sacrifice in their old profit-sharing ratio.

questions.question: On reconstitution, machinery (book value Rs. 1,50,000) is revalued at Rs. 1,30,000. This results in:
options: A) Loss of Rs. 20,000 debited to Revaluation
D) Profit of Rs. 20,000 credited to Revaluation
questions.explanation: Depreciation of Rs. 20,000 is debited to Revaluation Account as loss.

questions.question: E brings Rs. 25,000 as goodwill premium on admission. Old partners share profits 3:2. Old partner F share of goodwill is:
questions.explanation: Goodwill premium is distributed in sacrifice ratio (3:2). F gets 25,000 x 3/5 = Rs. 15,000.

questions.question: X and Y share profits 3:2 with capitals Rs. 90,000 and Rs. 60,000. Z is admitted for 1/4 share and brings Rs. 80,000 as capital. Total firm capital (as per Z) is:
questions.explanation: Z brings Rs. 80,000 for 1/4 share. Total implied capital = 80,000 x 4 = Rs. 3,20,000.

questions.question: A, B, C share profits 4:3:2. B retires. A and C acquire B share equally. The gaining ratio of A and C is:
questions.explanation: When B share is acquired equally by A and C, gaining ratio = 1:1.

questions.question: Debtors are Rs. 60,000. Provision for doubtful debts @ 10% is created for the first time. The revaluation entry is:
options: A) Debtors A/c Dr. 6,000; To Revaluation A/c 6,000
B) Provision A/c Dr. 6,000; To Revaluation A/c 6,000
D) Revaluation A/c Dr. 6,000; To Provision A/c 6,000
questions.explanation: New provision of Rs. 6,000 is debited to Revaluation (loss) and credited to Provision Account.

questions.question: P and Q have capitals of Rs. 1,20,000 and Rs. 80,000 sharing profits equally. R is admitted for 1/5 share bringing Rs. 50,000 as capital. The hidden goodwill is:
questions.explanation: R brings Rs. 50,000 for 1/5. Implied total = 50,000 x 5 = Rs. 2,50,000. Actual = Rs. 2,50,000. Goodwill = 0.

questions.question: Stock (Rs. 80,000) increased by 15%. Building (Rs. 3,00,000) decreased by 10%. Unrecorded creditors of Rs. 12,000 discovered. Net effect in Revaluation Account is:
questions.explanation: Stock gain = Rs. 12,000. Building loss = Rs. 30,000. Creditors = Rs. 12,000 loss. Net = 30,000 + 12,000 - 12,000 = Rs. 30,000 loss.

questions.question: X and Y have capitals of Rs. 80,000 and Rs. 60,000 sharing profits equally. Z is admitted for 1/4 share bringing Rs. 70,000 as capital. The hidden goodwill is:
questions.explanation: Z brings Rs. 70,000 for 1/4. Implied total = Rs. 2,80,000. Actual = Rs. 2,10,000. Goodwill = Rs. 70,000.

questions.question: Realisation Account is opened during:
questions.explanation: Realisation Account is opened at dissolution.

questions.question: On dissolution, assets (except cash) are transferred to Realisation Account at:
questions.explanation: All assets are transferred to Realisation Account at their book value.

questions.question: After paying realisation expenses, the first liability to be settled out of cash is:
questions.explanation: The order after realisation expenses: External debts, then partners loans, then capital.

questions.question: On dissolution, an unrecorded liability (audit fee) of Rs. 8,000 is paid. The journal entry is:
options: A) Realisation A/c Dr. 8,000; To Cash A/c 8,000
B) Cash A/c Dr. 8,000; To Realisation A/c 8,000
C) Partners Capital A/c Dr. 8,000; To Cash A/c 8,000
D) Audit Fee A/c Dr. 8,000; To Cash A/c 8,000
questions.explanation: Unrecorded liability paid is debited to Realisation Account and Cash is credited.

questions.question: On dissolution, partner R takes over furniture of book value Rs. 20,000 at agreed value of Rs. 16,000. The entry is:
options: A) Realisation A/c Dr. 20,000; To R Capital A/c 20,000
B) R Capital A/c Dr. 20,000; To Realisation A/c 20,000
C) R Capital A/c Dr. 16,000; To Realisation A/c 16,000
questions.explanation: When a partner takes over an asset, Partner Capital is debited with agreed value.

questions.question: A creditor of Rs. 35,000 is paid Rs. 33,000 in full settlement. The correct entry is:
options: A) Creditor A/c Dr. 35,000; To Cash A/c 33,000; To Partners Capital A/c 2,000
B) Realisation A/c Dr. 33,000; To Cash A/c 33,000
C) Realisation A/c Dr. 35,000; To Cash A/c 35,000
D) Creditor A/c Dr. 35,000; To Cash A/c 33,000; To Realisation A/c 2,000
questions.explanation: Creditor removed at Rs. 35,000. Discount of 2,000 is gain credited to Realisation.

questions.question: Partners J and K have capitals of Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 30,000. L is insolvent with debit balance of Rs. 16,000. Per Garner vs Murray, K bears additional loss of:
A, B, C share profits 3:2:1 with capitals Rs. 90,000, Rs. 60,000, Rs. 30,000. C is insolvent with capital deficiency of Rs. 24,000. Using Garner vs Murray, how much does A bear?
questions.explanation: Solvent partners capital ratio A:B = 90,000:60,000 = 3:2. A bears 3/5 x 24,000 = Rs. 14,400.

questions.question: The maximum amount of share capital a company can issue is called:
questions.explanation: Authorized capital is the maximum stated in the Memorandum of Association.

questions.question: Debenture holders are:
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are lenders/creditors who have given loans to the company.

questions.question: As per SEBI guidelines, minimum application money per share should not be less than:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates minimum application money of 25% of the issue price.

questions.question: 500 shares of Rs. 10 each are issued at Rs. 14 per share. Securities premium per share is:
questions.explanation: Issue price (Rs. 14) - Face value (Rs. 10) = Rs. 4 per share securities premium.

questions.question: A shareholder holding 100 shares of Rs. 10 each fails to pay allotment Rs. 5 and final call Rs. 2. Calls in Arrears is:
questions.explanation: Calls in Arrears = 100 x (5 + 2) = Rs. 700.

questions.question: 200 shares of Rs. 10 each (fully called) are forfeited. The shareholder had paid only application Rs. 4 per share. Forfeited Shares Account is credited with:
questions.explanation: Amount received = 200 x 4 = Rs. 800. This is credited to Forfeited Shares Account.

questions.question: Debentures issued as collateral security are recorded as:
options: A) Memorandum entry only (no journal entry)
B) Debentures Suspense A/c Dr. To Debentures A/c
C) Bank A/c Dr. To Debentures A/c
D) Interest A/c Dr. To Debentures A/c
questions.explanation: Collateral security debentures are not formally recorded in books.

questions.question: A company invited applications for 30,000 shares and received 60,000 applications. How many shares will an applicant who applied for 1,200 shares get?
questions.explanation: Pro-rata ratio = 30,000:60,000 = 1:2. Allotment = 1,200 x 1/2 = 600 shares.

questions.question: 150 shares of Rs. 10 each (fully called) were forfeited for non-payment of allotment Rs. 4 and final call Rs. 3. Shareholder paid application Rs. 3. These shares were reissued at Rs. 8 fully paid. Capital Reserve transferred is:
questions.explanation: Received on forfeited shares = 150 x 3 = Rs. 450. Loss on reissue = 150 x 2 = Rs. 300. Capital Reserve = 450 - 300 = Rs. 150.

questions.question: Quick Ratio is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities.

questions.question: Which is a non-current asset?
questions.explanation: Goodwill is an intangible non-current asset.

questions.question: Interest received by a non-financial company is classified as:
questions.explanation: For a non-financial company, interest received is classified as investing activity per AS-3.

questions.question: Current Ratio = 2:1 (CA = Rs. 80,000; CL = Rs. 40,000). Paid Rs. 20,000 to creditor. New Current Ratio is:
Shareholders Fund = Rs. 20,00,000. Total Debt = Rs. 30,00,000. Debt-Equity Ratio is:
questions.explanation: Debt-Equity Ratio = Total Debt / Shareholders Fund = 30,00,000 / 20,00,000 = 1.5:1.

questions.question: Cost of Revenue = Rs. 5,00,000. Opening Stock = Rs. 80,000. Closing Stock = Rs. 1,20,000. Inventory Turnover Ratio is:
Total Assets = Rs. 40,00,000. Total Debt = Rs. 16,00,000. Total Assets to Debt Ratio is:
questions.explanation: Total Assets to Debt Ratio = 40,00,000 / 16,00,000 = 2.5:1.

questions.question: Capital Employed = Rs. 50,00,000. Net Profit before Interest and Tax = Rs. 12,50,000. ROCE is:
Net Credit Purchases = Rs. 8,00,000. Opening Creditors = Rs. 2,00,000. Closing Creditors = Rs. 2,00,000. Trade Payables Turnover is:
questions.explanation: Average Creditors = Rs. 2,00,000. Turnover = 8,00,000 / 2,00,000 = 4 times.

questions.question: The most widely used accounting software package in India is:
questions.explanation: Tally is the most popular accounting software in India.

questions.question: DBMS stands for:
questions.explanation: DBMS = Database Management System — software to manage databases.

questions.question: Which is a key advantage of computerised accounting over manual accounting?
options: B) Speed and accuracy in processing transactions
C) No need for accounting knowledge
questions.explanation: Computerised systems offer speed, accuracy, and automatic report generation.

questions.question: In computerised accounting, regular data backup is needed because:
options: A) Data can be lost due to system failure or corruption
C) It reduces the need for accountants
D) It is required for every transaction
questions.explanation: Backups protect against data loss from hardware failure, software crashes, or accidental deletion.

questions.question: Codification of accounts in a computerised system helps in:
options: C) Systematic grouping and easy identification
questions.explanation: Codification assigns unique codes to accounts for systematic grouping and easy identification.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about audit trail in computerised accounting?
options: A) It may be limited and needs special programming to track changes
B) It is always superior to manual
D) It is not required by law
questions.explanation: Computerised systems may lack built-in audit trails; special features must be programmed.

questions.question: A major limitation of a highly customized accounting package is:
options: C) Not suitable for large firms
D) High cost and longer implementation time
questions.explanation: Customized packages require significant investment in development and implementation time.
